A highly symmetrical illustration depicts a large fantastical moth against a textured, aged parchment background. The insect fills most of the vertical composition with its four wings fully spread. Its palette is dominated by dense black, charcoal gray, muted cream, and vivid blood red. The upper wings contain enormous concentric circular markings resembling staring eyes, with red rings surrounding dark centers. Smaller red spots and intricate black linework cover the wings, while the lower pair taper downward in long, dark panels edged and spotted with crimson. At the center, the moth has glossy red compound eyes, feathery antennae sweeping upward and outward, and a heavily segmented black-and-red abdomen. Its thorax contains skull-like and mask-like markings that give the insect an unsettling, almost vampiric face. Above the antennae floats a separate red iris and black pupil surrounded by a roughly drawn eye, glowing amid a spray of red pigment. A second matching eye appears below the moth, followed by a tiny, realistically proportioned moth near the bottom edge. Loose black flecks and red splatters surround the central figure, reinforcing the appearance of an occult natural-history plate drawn in ink on old paper.
